caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 1413 of 2005.
lawyer:
For the Petitioners: Mr. T: H. Khan, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record. 
For Respondent : Not Represented.
parties:
Ali Hossain, and others ------ Petitioners 
-Versus-
The Chairman, First Court of Settlement and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Matin, J.- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.08.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2645 of 2001 discharging the Rule challenging the judgment and order dated 11.03.2001 passed by the 1st Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka in Case No. 97 of 1987 (KhaS), Lalmatia, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. 

2. The petitioner filed the Writ Petition No.2645 of 2001 before the High Court Division challenging inclusion of the building at 3/9, Block-F, Lalmatia, Mohammadpur, Dhaka in Bangladesh Gazette 'Kha' dated 23.09.1986 published under Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance 54/85 at page No.9764(20) serial No.5 as well as judgment and order dated 11.03.2001 passed by the 1st Court' of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka in Case No.97 of 1987. 
3. The facts, in short, are that the aforesaid plot of land upon which the disputed building situated was originally allotted to SK. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum by an allotment order dated 30.03.1967 by the then Government of East Pakistan and subsequently a lease deed dated 27.06.1967 was registered between the Government of East Pakistan on the one hand and SK. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum on the other. That after allotment order and registration of lease deed the original owners Sk. Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum took delivery of possession of the aforesaid Building and began to own, possess and live therein by paying Government clues and the cost of the plot of land without any interruption from any quarter. 

4. After Liberation War the original owner Sk. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum were in need of raising case money for their business and for paying installments of the cost of the house and accordingly they concluded a bainanama with Sk. Shafazuddin Ahamed on 15.10.1973 for the sale of the suit property and handed over delivery of possession to Sk. Shafazuddin on the same day that is on 15.10.1973. Thereafter, a clearance certificate for the payment of the full cost of the suit property was issued by the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement on 13.03.1975 and that it was stipulated in the bainanama that the vendor Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum will execute and register the sale deed within one year after completion of the formalities by themselves and when the vendor failed to do so the purchaser Sk. Shafazuddin Ahmed was constrained to file a suit being Title Suit No.22 of 1975 for specific performance of contract in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Court, Dhaka. 

5. The Government as defendant appeared on 15.01.1975 in the aforesaid suit and prayed for time by a petition for filing written statement but at last the G.P. did not contest the case because he could not procure the relevant connected papers and para-wise statements from the Ministry concerned and hence the suit was decreed ex-parte on 23.12.1977. After an. ex-parte decree a sale deed being No.40563 dated 21.11.1978 was executed and registered through court in favour of Sk. Shafazuddin, the purchaser. After ex-parte decree and registration of the aforesaid sale deed the Government preferred a Miscellaneous Case being No.159 of 1986 but .subsequently the said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default on 21.01.1989. Against the said order the Government did not take any step before the higher court. 

6. After decree and registration of the sale deed through court while the purchaser Shafazuddin has been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building, his name was recorded during R.S. operation and that while the purchaser has been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building without any interruption from any quarter he applied to the Assistant Commissioner of the House and Settlement of the Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka for mutating his name in place of the earlier owners and in reply the Assistant Commissioner by his letter dated 05.07.1982 asked the purchaser Shafazuddin Ahammed to submit the lease deed, purchase deed, plaint and decree of the court. Thereafter Shafazuddin submitted the aforesaid documents in writing to the Assistant Commissioner. 

7. On 24.03.1982 the Housing and Settlement Officer of the Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka published a show cause notice to the allottee of Lalmatia Housing Estate about the 'construction of their respective allotted plot and the purchaser Shafazuddin gave a reply in writing on 20.08.1982 to that show cause notice and Shafazuddin Ahmed completed the construction of building within two years.- In the aforesaid circumstances while Shafazuddin Ahamed had been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building the section officer Moksud Ahammed by his Memo No.9/124 dated 20.01.1986 asked him to show his documents in support of his occupation and in reply he submitted his documents in writing explaining, inter-alia, that he purchased the building from its original owners Sk. Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum and since then he is in possession of the aforesaid building and he has also applied earlier to the Assistant Commissioner of the Housing and Settlement of the Ministry of Works for mutating his name along with all the documents. 

 8. The building in question was enlisted in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 23.09.1986 as per provision of the Ordinance 54/85 whereupon the petitioner filed a petition in the First Court of Settlement for release of the building under Section 7 of the Ordinance 54/85. The aforesaid petition was registered as Case No.97 of 1987 in the First Court of Settlement. The Court of Settlement without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record illegally rejected the aforesaid case on 11.03.2001. Thereafter the petitioner filed writ petition as aforesaid and the High Court Division passed the impugned order discharging the Rule issued earlier and hence this petition. 
9. Heard the learned Counsel and perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record. 

10. Then learned Counsel for the petitioners submit that the High Court Division treated the letter issued by the Section Officer (vide Annexure-`K' to the writ petition) as statutory notice under section 5(1) (b) of the ordinance No.54 of 1985 but this finding is not correct as it is not in inconformity with the form 11 referred to in Rule 3 of the Rules for the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Taking over Possession) Rules, 1972 framed under the provision of Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and disposal) Order, 1972, the letter so issued is no notice in the eye of law and as such the findings of the High Court Division in respect of mandatory statutory notice is without lawful authority and are liable to be set aside. 

11. The learned Counsel has referred to the cases of Bangladesh Vs. Kazi Ashrafuddin Ahmed reported in 23 BLD(AD) 2003 Page-49 and Bangladesh Vs. Amela Khatoon others reported in 53 DLR(AD) 2001 Page-55. 

12. The learned Counsel further submits that when a bainanama is proved in a competent court of law in a case in which the Government was a party and the case is decreed in favour of the petitioner and the Government filed Miscellaneous Case No.159 of 1986 against the decree which was dismissed for default and the Government did not go to the higher court, the court of settlement has no jurisdiction to require the bainanama to be proved before them as the decree is binding upon them. 

13. It appears that the High Court Division considered Section 4 of the Ordinance No.54 of 1985 and 5(1) (b) of the Ordinance and held: 
"According to the said provision a notice in any from is required to be issued under P.0.16 of 1972 on or before the 31s` day of March, 1986 in case enlisting a property as abandoned property under "Kha" list which will be published under Section 5(1) (b) of the Ordinance 54 of 1985." 

The notice as in exhibit-K is dated 20.01.1986 long before 31.03.1986 and has been rightly held to be a valid notice in respect of a property which is an abandoned property as per provision of P.0.16 of 1972. The question whether or not the vendor of the petitioner was holding processing and managing the property in question on 28 February of 1972 is the pertinent question which has not been answered by the petitioner whose title allegedly accrued on the basis of a hainapatra dated 15.10.1973. The subsequent suit for specific performance of contract and the decree in the suit is of no avail to the petitioner inasmuch as the very status of the land and building in question as abandoned property was not decided in the suit. 

14. The petitioner could not prove the possession of his vendor on 28 February, 1972 and therefore the Court of Settlement rightly rejected the settlement case and the High Court Division correctly discharged the Rule. 

15. In the facts and circumstances of this case the decisions reported in 23 BLD(AD) 49 or 53 DLR(AD) 55 have no manner application in the instant case. The proposition of law has been settled by this court in the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Jalil and others reported in 48 DLR(AD)10 where it has been laid down that the onus, is squarely on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant. 

16. This Court also decided the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and held that the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution can interfere with the findings of a tribunal of fact only if it can be shown that the tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence/facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted malafide or in violation of any principle of natural justice. 

17. We find no merit in this petition which is accordingly dismissed. 

End.
